newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds close on rally, outperform after data.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds close on rally, outperform after data.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed much stronger on Friday, outperforming their U.S. counterparts, amid firm foreign buying, a stronger currency and speculation of another Bank of Canada rate cut, analysts said.

"There's no scenario that you come up with that isn't positive for Canada," said Barry Allan, vice-president of global fixed income with Altamira Investment Services. "If the Fed is on hold then the Bank of Canada basically has free rein to lower rates to wherever they want."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$1.55 to C$106.80 to yield 7.410 percent.
The U.S. 30-year benchmark gained 1 6/32 to yield 6.74 percent. The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to 67 basis points from 70 basis points at Thursday's close.

The rally in Canadian bonds stems largely from a U.S. Labor Department report released this morning which showed U.S. nonfarm payrolls fell 40,000 in September. Economists had forecast a rise of 166,000.

Analysts said data decreased expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve will increase interest rates at its next meeting. The report prompted strong buying of both Canadian bonds and the dollar by foreigners, dealers said.
"With today's employment numbers in the U.S., prospects for another Bank of Canada ease have opened up again," said Craig Wright, deputy chief economist with the Royal Bank of Canada.
Dealers said gains in the currency were driven partly by fund managers attracted by the unit's strong fundamentals.
In other prices, the 7.0 percent of 2006 rose C$1.34 to C$101.89 to yield 6.739 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark rose 26/32 to yield 6.49 percent.
The spread between the two benchmark bonds narrowed to 25 basis points from 34 basis points at Thursday's close.
The three-month cash bill traded at 3.48 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.01 percent.
